transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My name is Baha, I'm a 37-year-old firefighter, and I've been struggling a lot with my focus lately. When I’m not on an actual call, I just can’t keep my attention on training, reports, or manuals long enough to get through them properly, which is really stalling my coursework for a promotion to captain.
Have you struggled with these difficulties in maintaining focus or staying organized since you were a child, or is this a more recent change in your life?

These issues really came to a head about a year and a half ago when I started my captaincy coursework, but they actually go all the way back to childhood. Even in elementary school, teachers constantly moved my seat because I wouldn't stop talking, and I'd regularly forget to turn in homework I had actually completed. My report cards always noted that I was smart but just couldn't sit still or stay focused in class.
Besides the difficulty with focus, do you often find yourself feeling restless, needing to be constantly on the go, or acting impulsively without thinking through the consequences?

Yes, absolutely—my crew actually jokes that I'm "powered by batteries" because I'm constantly pacing or organizing gear, and if I'm forced to sit still, I get this pent-up, crawling feeling inside. I also struggle with impulsivity, like constantly cutting people off in conversations or blurting out answers before the instructor even finishes the question. It really feels like I'm always on the go and can't seem to slow my brain or body down.
Do you find that these symptoms of inattention and restlessness are present in multiple settings, such as both at work and in your personal life at home?

Yes, it definitely affects my personal life just as much as my work. At home, I'm constantly forgetting to call my wife back or missing bill payments that are sitting right on the counter. I also can't even sit still to watch a movie with my son without constantly fidgeting or getting up because I feel so restless.

Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually energized, slept very little for days, or engaged in uncharacteristically risky behavior that was different from your usual restless baseline?

No, I've never experienced distinct periods like that. While I'm always restless and on the go as my normal baseline, I don't have phases where I go days without sleep or do things that are totally uncharacteristic or unusually risky for me.
